chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who testified upon the testimony of another man, then the man came and said: “Indeed, I did not make him a witness.”
He عليه السلام said: “The testimony of the more upright of the two is accepted, and if their uprightness is equal, his testimony is not accepted.”

key_terms.أَعْدَلِهِمَا: the more upright of the two
key_terms.أُشْهِدْهُ: I did not appoint him as a witness

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a witness testifies on another man’s testimony and the original man denies authorizing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about conflicting testimony when one person testifies based on another person’s attestation, and the original person later denies having authorized it. The ruling gives preference to the testimony of the more upright witness; if both are equal in uprightness, the secondary testimony is not accepted. It reflects the importance of justice and reliability in judicial matters.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3353 - It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdurrahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (as)
regarding a man who testified based on the testimony of another man, and then the original man said: 'I did not make him a witness,'
Imam (as) said: "The testimony of the more upright of the two is accepted, but if their uprightness is equal, then his testimony is not accepted."
